newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Bogota marchers protest political disappearances.
newsitem.headline: Bogota marchers protest political disappearances.

text.p: Several hundred demonstrators staged a torchlit march through downtown Bogota on Friday in protest at disappearances they blame on the Colombian state security services and illegal right-wing death squads.

About 300 protesters, including international delegates from Turkey, Bosnia and elsewhere in Europe, snarled rush-hour traffic, chanting slogans and waving banners with mottoes such as "State terrorism disappears, kills and jails."

Independent human rights groups estimate at least two people are abducted each day by Colombia's police or military and not returned, and that more than 3,500 people have disappeared since the late 1970s.

"There's nothing we can do about the disappeared and the tortured because they're already gone. But we're here in the hope that this type of thing will not continue," said Manuel Rodriguez, a leader of the state telephone workers' union.

The march marked the start of a three-day international conference organised by the International Committee Against Disappearances and is backed by a wide range of Colombian social groups and leftist organisations, whose members are frequently singled out for attack as political troublemakers.
